answer: Make each identity rent its own network position. A key must answer a monthly liveness probe from a routing vertex it has never used, relayed by two unrelated providers picked at random. Results land in a public vault that pays only after thirty days of settlements with distinct counterparties; clones answering from one rack collapse into a single vertex and their vault stays frozen. Because the probe shows where a key truly sits, a lonely knoll rather than a shared valley, a thousand copies need a thousand footholds plus real trade, which scripting cannot compress.
